video_title: Full Denver Nuggets Postgame Media Availability vs. TOR 🎙

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on managing Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon's minutes
quotes.excerpt: This is a team, and the team has to help each other out with the minutes.
quotes.quote: To accomplish that, other people have to play well. I thought the second unit was great. The best thing about it was the continuation of the momentum of the guys that came in. There wasn't really a step back, they just kept coming. The activity remained the same. This is a team, and the team has to help each other out with the minutes. It's not just me just guessing if we can win a game. Jamal plays 28, 29, so it came at the right time. Jamal's played a lot. Obviously, Aaron, we'd like to keep him at a threshold, but I was proud of the energy in the second half.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on managing Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon minutes: It is not just me guessing if we can win a game. Jamal plays 28, 29, so it came at the right time. Jamal has played a lot.

structured.context: Coach Adelman discusses his strategy for managing the minutes of Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon during the game.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on Christian Braun's development and earned trust
quotes.excerpt: The nights that Christian Braun has not played, there's been no lack of trust.
quotes.quote: The nights that Christian Braun has not played, there's been no lack of trust. He's earned this in the preseason, but it's just the steadiness every day. That's in player development, that's when he watches film with his coach, the guys that we assign to these players. That's the feeling you get from a player every day. When somebody is a consistent person on top of the fact that they know who they are and they're on the court, that goes a long way where I don't really skip a beat. Jamal's out, okay, let's, it's Christian, let's give him a chance.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on Christian Braun: The nights that Christian Braun has not played, there has been no lack of trust. He has earned this in the preseason, but it is just the steadiness every day.

structured.context: Coach Adelman explains how Christian Braun has earned his trust through consistent development and preparation.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman compares Christian Braun's playstyle to a running back
quotes.excerpt: He looks for contact, doesn't dance, just goes straight ahead.
quotes.quote: He reminds me of a north-south running back. He looks for contact, doesn't dance, just goes straight ahead. It's like knowing your own game. He made the first three to start, which I think loosened him up a little bit. My favorite play from Christian the whole night, the outlet pass, he dropped. A lot of times, you finally get to play, you make a three, you're feeling momentum, then you drop the ball out of bounds. I didn't see a reaction to that. He just kept playing.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on Christian Braun: He reminds me of a north-south running back. He looks for contact, does not dance, just goes straight ahead.

structured.context: Coach Adelman describes Christian Braun's aggressive playstyle by comparing him to a north-south running back.

quotes.speaker: Nikola Jokic
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic on his aggressive start to the game
quotes.excerpt: I never played the game in future, I always play in the present.
quotes.quote: It just happened, you know, I didn't mean to do, I mean, it just happens for me, you know. I never played the game in future, I always play in the present, and if something happens, I'm going to try to take advantage or if I have, if I'm open, I'm going to try to shoot it, and it was a good night for me.
quotes.social_post: Nikola Jokic on his aggressive start: I never played the game in future, I always play in the present, and if something happens, I am going to try to take advantage.

quotes.speaker: Nikola Jokic
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic on the lack of size advantage in today's NBA
quotes.excerpt: In today's NBA, I think there is no size advantage.
quotes.quote: In today's NBA, I think there is no size advantage just because in the low post, I think we have a lot of defenders or player on the post and defensive side can do much more, pushing, grabbing, whatever, than if you're playing outside. I think that's why players are not willing to play in the low post anymore, you know, it's just because you're going to get a foul and it's never going to get called and you're getting tired after possession. I think that's why the low post is kind of in the hand zone, like I think probably next 5-10 years, low post is not going to even be up there, so that's why the people are trying to put smaller.
quotes.social_post: Nikola Jokic on the state of the low post: I think probably next 5-10 years, low post is not going to even be up there, so that is why the people are trying to put smaller.

structured.context: Nikola Jokic shares his perspective on why the low post position is becoming less common in the modern NBA.

quotes.speaker: Tyus Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyus Jones on Christian Braun's confidence and impact
quotes.excerpt: I think this is the confidence that he played with. He came in and made an impact.
quotes.quote: I think this is the confidence that he played with. He came in and made an impact right away. He didn't wait or try to feel the game out, and that's just a testament to his work that he's been putting in, staying ready.
quotes.social_post: Tyus Jones on Christian Braun: He came in and made an impact right away. He did not wait or try to feel the game out, and that is just a testament to his work that he has been putting in.

quotes.speaker: Tyus Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyus Jones on gauging his impact on the game
quotes.excerpt: First thing for me typically is plus-minus. I want our unit to be at least even.
quotes.quote: First thing for me typically is plus-minus. I want our unit to be at least even. You know, that's something that I've learned early in my career, especially you know coming off the bench is you want to try as best as you can to be, you know, plus, if not even. You know, and obviously the game is up and downs, there's a game of runs, you can't control substitution patterns and things like that. So sometimes it's out of your control, but that's the first thing. Then for me, assist to turnover is huge, taking care of the ball. Our minutes are lower, so you got to be more efficient, you know, with with, you know, less less possession, less minutes.
quotes.social_post: Tyus Jones on his metrics: First thing for me typically is plus-minus. I want our unit to be at least even. Then for me, assist to turnover is huge, taking care of the ball.

structured.context: Tyus Jones explains the metrics he uses to evaluate his own performance as a reserve player.
